items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: with the exceptions of the greats Ella, Sarah, Joe Williams, Billy Eckstine, recent Diana Reeves, Cassandra Wilson, Kevin Mahogany

ctx.x: Because you’d like to know something about the person. Because see again, a theory I have, that’s why talk shows were invented, for the actors. Because you see an actor on stage, or in a film, he’s playing someone from the eighteenth century, and someone from the twenty-fifth century in another film, and he’s a good guy in this film and he’s a bad guy in that film. Okay. But you don’t know nothing about the person. So my own theory is that that’s why the talk shows came in. Because now you can see this actor that…

having. Okay I think this dialogue helps to do that but there’s not enough of it. Okay? And we have the opportunity even on stage to do that. And most of us don’t take that opportunity. And also, because the fact that it is a primarily instrumental medium it makes us less accessible. Because all the other genres are vocally driven.
